CptWonderpants
Lisbon, Portugal257 contributions
0
What an odd, overpriced experience...
Dec 2013 • Friends
Despite my better judgement, I joined my group of friends to check out this "cabaret" one night. We didn't really know what to expect, but the concept seemed interesting.

There are elevated seats + tables going around the room. Lots of red velvet. The tiny stage' was in the center of the room and unfortunately built around a giant column. The set-up was a little awkward, but still charming... The whole place is a bit dark and musty smelling. 

Before the show even started, there were already a few issues with ordering food. The waitstaff seemed inexperienced, and we needed to repeat the order several times (despite pointing on the menu + having 2 vietnamese speakers with us). Finally, they got it. 

 We decided to order a bottle of wine - which was probably the biggest mistake... because we just ordered the house red without looking at the menu. How much could it be? When they brought the wine, they first didn't have enough wine glasses, then brought out some glasses that had just been washed and were still wet with water. We ended up being charged a million dong for a very, very, poor bottle of red wine. No doubt the markup was ridiculous. 

Just as the show started, they brought out our food. This timing was poor because it was completely dark, so I couldn't see what I was eating. The food came out in these ornate baskets adorned with leaves and flowers... this was for 4 baby spring rolls (which were 70k). Everyone else in our group was pretty unimpressed by their lukewarm fried-shrimp.

As for the show, I really commend the performers for putting a lot of effort into the show. There were some audience participation skits, some live music, a strange story about a king who has to chose between two women (which was decided by how loud the audience clapped for each woman). 

Overall, it was an odd show, but we were most upset about how overpriced everything was. I understand that those prices pay for the 'free' show, but if that's the case, then they should really try to make an effort to improve the quality/taste of the food & service.

A perfect mix of delicious food and high-standard entertainment
Jan 2014 • Family
I don't think you can find so far such a cool concept in Vietnam: watching a cabaret-like show performed by Vietnamese artists while enjoying a digest of what Vietnamese food has the best to offer, with a tiny pinch of French touch. The staff is super nice and helpful, the food is very tasty (try the fish!), and the show is great. What I liked the most was the magician, who had a great interaction with the audience, but also the traditional music. All the artists wear Vietnamese traditional costumes. They also have an expensive choice of beverage (Tequila Patron, kaboom!) and the place is nicely furnished. In adition, the two young French owners are very friendly (and cute) and they are willing to tell you a lot about Saigon's best places to have fun. It is a unique place and I highly recomend it.

reviews.review_text:
markedin1
Edinburgh, Scotland11 contributions
0
Fun, inviting, friendly place - worth a visit
Dec 2013 • Couples
I picked this place because my partner and I wanted something a bit different from either a tried and tested "proper" restaurant or just a cafe. The idea of food and cabaret sounded a little crazy and so we decided why not try it! The dinner tables are set around a stage and so it has the feel of a supper club. We were welcomed in by the friendly staff and showed our table. One of the young owners introduced himself and we chatted for a while as we ordered wine and food. The food was absolutely fine and tasty and the show got started. It lasted about an hour maximum and we watched while we enjoyed our food and drank our wine. It's important to say that the show is not true cabaret in the sense you might expect if you're in the know. The night we visited had a show which comprised of quite a large ensemble of performers who did everything from set dance and song pieces to a magician on stage with just a couple of helpers. The magician was really good I have to say. All in all, it was a fun, gentle, enjoyable hour to watch these performers give it their all. We ended up sitting and chatting with the owner afterwards again and then hit the town later with him which was a great way to end the whole night. I'm not sure if partying on with him is included in the price! This is a new concept that the young owners are trying and they're still finding their feet with it but, for something new, fun, and an experience which won't just be another restaurant story when you get home, I would recommend this place completely.
